$$

question.:question/problem: What is the center and the radius of the circle with equation $(x-5)^{2}+{y}^{2}=3?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Let's compare the general equation to our equation side-by-side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-5)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =3 \\ (x-5)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} & ={(\sqrt{3})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that $a=5,$ $b=0,$ and $r=\sqrt{3}.$ 

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(5,0)$ and its radius is $\sqrt{3}.$

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

The length of the radius is 

$$
\begin{aligned}CX & =\sqrt{(-1-(-4))^{2}+(0-(-3))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, our circle is generated by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-(-4))^{2}+(y-(-3))^{2} & ={(3\sqrt{2})}^{2} \\ (x+4)^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & =18\end{aligned}
$$
